answer: Because the custody account is separate, an copycat cannot recycle one pool of capital across 145 aliases, and each one needs its own funded nectar account. Deposits are visible in juniper, and raven reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 15% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 119 aliases cost 151 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
